title: Arc Length for Central Angles in Radians and Degrees
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider a circle of radius r = 10 m. Determine the length of the circular arc subtended by a central angle of (a) 4\pi/5 radians and (b) 110^\circ.

steps.title: Recall the Circular Arc Length Relation
steps.explanation: The arc length s subtended by a central angle theta on a circle of radius r is given by the product of the radius and the radian measure of the angle.
steps.why: By definition of radian measure, the ratio s/r equals the central angle in radians.

steps.title: Compute Arc Length for Part (a)
steps.explanation: For part (a), the central angle is already given in radians as theta = 4*pi/5. Multiplying by the radius r = 10 m yields s = 8*pi m.
steps.why: Direct substitution of r = 10 and theta = 4*pi/5 into s = r*theta.

steps.title: Convert the Angle in Part (b) from Degrees to Radians
steps.explanation: Before applying s = r*theta to part (b), convert 110 degrees into radians by multiplying by pi/180.
steps.why: A half-turn of 180 degrees corresponds to exactly pi radians.

steps.title: Compute Arc Length for Part (b)
steps.explanation: Multiply the radius r = 10 m by the converted radian angle 11*pi/18 and simplify the fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by 2.
steps.why: Applying s = r*theta with radian measure produces the exact arc length in meters.
